plain.text: Pharisees tested Jesus with a question about divorce. Jesus pointed back to creation: God made them male and female, and the two become one flesh, so what God has joined, no one should separate. Moses allowed divorce because hearts were hard, but it was not so from the beginning. Jesus said divorce and remarriage, except for sexual unfaithfulness, is adultery. He added that some remain single for the sake of the kingdom.

People brought little children for Jesus to bless, and the disciples told them off. Jesus said, Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these. He placed his hands on them.

A young man asked what good thing he must do to get eternal life. Jesus told him to keep the commandments. He said he had; what did he still lack? Jesus said: sell your possessions, give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me. The young man went away sad, because he was very rich. Jesus said it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom. The disciples were astonished: who then can be saved? With man this is impossible, Jesus said, but with God all things are possible. Everyone who has left things for his sake will receive far more, and the first will be last and the last first.

summary.bigIdea: Jesus welcomes children and shows that entering God's kingdom is not something we can earn or buy: with God all things are possible.
points: Jesus upholds marriage as God's design.
A rich young man cannot let go of his wealth to follow Jesus.
summary.reflection: Is there something you are holding onto that makes it hard to follow Jesus freely?
